meaning:
μετα-βαίνω
[in LXX: Wis.7:27 19:19, 2Ma.6:1 2Mac 6:9 2Mac 6:24 * ;]
to pass over from one place to another : Mat.17:20, Luk.10:7; with reference to the point of departure only, to withdraw, depart: Mat.8:34 11:1 12:9 15:29, Jhn.7:3, Act.18:7; of removal from this life, ἐκ τ. κότμου πρὸς τ. Πατέρα, Jhn.13:1; metaphorically, ἐκ τ. θανάτου εἰς τ. ζωήν, Jhn.5:24, 1Jn.3:14.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.
Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go from house to house.
“Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death…
He departed there, and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.
